name: Repeated practice of the principles (tattvābhyāsa)
method_summary: After hearing the principles (manifest, unmanifest, knower) from scripture and teacher and establishing them by reasoning, one contemplates them repeatedly — long, reverently and without interruption — discriminating puruṣa from each principle and renouncing identification with each ('not this, not this'), until the knowledge 'I am not, not mine, not I' arises.
prerequisites: hearing and reasoning about the twenty-five principles; dispassion
duration: long and uninterrupted; Vācaspati speaks of many births of practice
signs_of_progress: the complete, pure, single knowledge 'I am not, not mine, not I' (SK 64); prakṛti seen as by a spectator, having ceased (SK 65–66)

warnings.text: Liberation is not attained by mere hearing, because beginningless latent tendencies are strong.
Dispassion without discrimination leads only to absorption in prakṛti, from which one rises again.

equivalents.note: long uninterrupted contemplation after hearing and reflection, as in Advaita's nididhyāsana; content and goal differ (discrimination vs identity)

name: The means-accomplishments: study, hearing, reasoning, friends, giving
method_summary: Five of the eight accomplishments of SK 51 serve as means to knowledge of the principles: studying the texts, hearing instruction, examining by reasoning ('what is true, what is highest, what is the final good'), gaining a friend or fellow student who knows, and serving the venerable with gifts (Gauḍapāda) — Vācaspati (recalled) reads dāna as the purification of discriminative knowledge. Approaching a teacher to end the three sufferings is itself an accomplishment.
prerequisites: desire to know born of suffering (SK 1)
signs_of_progress: knowledge of the twenty-five principles arises

warnings.text: Error, incapacity and contentment are the curb that holds the world in ignorance like a goaded elephant; they must be abandoned.
Hearing without reflection does not bring fulfilment, as with Virocana.

name: Dispassion (vairāgya)
method_summary: Turning away from objects by seeing the faults of acquiring, guarding, losing, attachment and harm (external dispassion), and seeing even pradhāna as like a dream or magic show (internal dispassion); with practice, a support of meditation.
signs_of_progress: calming of passion; freedom from expectation (like Piṅgalā, SS 4.11)

warnings.text: Through dispassion (alone) comes absorption into prakṛti, not liberation.
External contentment from abstaining from objects, without knowledge of the principles, does not liberate.

name: Seeing the faults (doṣa-darśana)
method_summary: Reflecting on the faults in acquiring, guarding and losing objects, in attachment, and in the harm enjoyment does to beings, so that passion subsides; passion is not quieted by enjoyment but by seeing the faults of both.

warnings.text: Abstaining from objects for these faults is only a contentment, not liberation, without knowledge of the principles.

name: Meditation as objectless mind (dhyāna)
method_summary: Meditation is the removal of passion, accomplished through the cessation of the mind's modifications; meditation is mind without object; supported by concentration, posture, one's own duty, dispassion and practice, turning away from torpor and distraction, in any place where the mind is serene.
signs_of_progress: coloring of puruṣa calmed, puruṣa abiding in itself like a crystal (SS 2.34–35)

warnings.text: Torpor and distraction are to be turned away from.

name: Posture (āsana)
method_summary: Sāṃkhya contribution: posture is whatever is steady and pleasant; there is no fixed rule.

name: Concentration (dhāraṇā)
method_summary: Sāṃkhya contribution: concentration, with posture and one's own duty, accomplishes meditation (SS 3.32); with meditation, practice and dispassion it stops the coloring of puruṣa (SS 6.29).

name: Breath restraint (prāṇāyāma)
method_summary: Sāṃkhya contribution: restraint (of breath) by expulsion and retention, as a support of meditation (SS 3.33); no further detail is given in the sūtra.

name: Performing one's own duty (svakarma)
method_summary: One's own duty is performing the acts enjoined for one's stage of life; with concentration and posture it supports meditation (SS 3.32, 3.35).

name: 'Not this, not this' (neti neti)
method_summary: Sāṃkhya contribution: discrimination is accomplished through practice of the principles by giving up each with 'not this, not this' (SS 3.76).
